subject: Reserved-capacity drain / 5xx + latency spike — immediate mitigation & exec standby
messages:
From: Cara Nguyen <cara.nguyen@clearcore.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout latency + 5xx — reserved throughput being consumed

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

We're seeing a sudden latency spike (p95 ~1.3s up from ~120ms) on our Checkout API and a ~6% 5xx rate starting ~08:50 PDT. Our Grafana and ClearCore's own telemetry show tokens being consumed from the reserved capacity much faster than expected — QPS looks steady but token-per-request has jumped. This is causing timeouts in our payment step and a few failed transactions.

Attached screenshots and a sample stacktrace (checkout_stacktrace_20260812.txt). Critical business impact: ~10% of Checkout requests are failing right now. We're on a reserved plan and need immediate mitigation or direction on fallback.

Can you confirm:
- Are you seeing a saturated dedicated pool for our reservation?
- Is there an immediate mitigation you can flip (model fallback / rate limiting / burst authorization)?

We appreciate urgency — our ops team is standing by.

Thanks,
Cara Nguyen
Head of SRE & Payments
ClearCore Payments

Cara — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. We see the same signal in our telemetry: a sudden increase in token-cost-per-call for your model route starting ~08:46 PDT which exhausted the per-reservation token buffer earlier than expected. QPS is within expected but the avg tokens/request doubled for a short window.

Immediate actions I'm taking now (ETA in parentheses):
- Promote the lightweight fallback model (quantized v1) for the Checkout route — this will reduce token cost and should drop p95 latency (rolling in ~5m).
- Apply a temporary route-level rate cap to protect the reserved pool while we stabilize (will not fully throttle, just headroom preservation).
- Opened JIRA INF-1279 to track remediation and post-mortem.

Priyom / Vivek — I need confirmation on authorizing an emergency burst (dedicated pool oversubscribe) while we stabilize. ClearCore is on a reserved contract but we will need a one-time buffer allocation to prevent user-impact while fallback completes.

Cara / Suresh — we'll keep you updated every 15 minutes until nominal. Expect the first mitigation (fallback promotion) in the next 5 minutes.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Incident Lead, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — quick triage notes and recommended mitigation path: 

Triage summary (observed):
- Dedicated pool assigned to ClearCore shows kernel-level slowdowns for long-sequence requests; token cost per request spiked due to a small set of atypical inputs (we have sample payloads).
- KV cache miss rate increased (cache TTL recently tightened in a prior deploy).
- No evidence of hardware failure; this looks workload-driven.

Immediate mitigations (to execute now):
1) Promote quantized lightweight model on the route (Jonas is doing this). Expected impact: ~40-55% token reduction and lower p95. ETA 5–7m.
2) Temporarily relax cache TTL for your route to reduce cold KV misses (ops to apply now). ETA 10m.
3) Authorize a limited burst: allow +30% capacity on the dedicated pool for 60 minutes as a safety valve while we stabilize. We will cut the burst once metrics return to baseline.

Authorization ask: 
- Approve burst for ClearCore (one-time). We should route billing through the reserved buffer and consider a small operational credit.

I'll coordinate the deploy steps. Jon, loop me into the bridge with ClearCore for sign-off on the fallback.

— Priyom
Director, Customer Reliability

Cara / Suresh — quick update and closure note for the immediate incident: 

What we applied: 
- Promoted quantized lightweight model for the Checkout route at 09:33 PDT. Latency and token-per-request quickly improved.
- Relaxed the route cache TTL (reduced cold miss rate) at 09:42 PDT.
- Authorized a limited +30% burst on the dedicated pool for 60 minutes (confirmed). Burst was never fully consumed; reserved headroom returned to normal by ~10:25 PDT.

Impact: 
- P95 reduced back to ~140ms within ~10 minutes of the fallback promotion.
- 5xx rate dropped from ~6% to <0.5% across the hour.

Next steps: 
- We will run an RCA and post-mortem (JIRA INF-1279) focused on: cache TTL settings, model selection guidance, and safety thresholds for token-cost anomalies.
- Vivek proposed a one-time $5k operational credit to ClearCore; Lauren, please advise on approval flow.
- We'll follow up with a proposed model/quantization recommendation and a recommended reserved delta if ClearCore wants a wider safety buffer.

Suresh / Cara — apologies for the disruption. We know this hits checkout hard; happy to jump on a bridge with your ops team to go over the timeline and the fix.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Incident Lead, Customer Escalations
